newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesians among E.Timor activist deportees.
newsitem.headline: Indonesians among E.Timor activist deportees.

text.p: Nine Indonesians were among the foreign activists Malaysia was expected to deport after they took part in a controversial weekend conference on East Timor in Kuala Lumpur, an Amnesty International official said on Sunday.
Immigration authorities in Kuala Lumpur said on Sunday they were deporting a number of foreign activists who had attended the abortive meeting at a hotel in the Malaysian capital on Saturday.
Youths from groups allied to Malaysia's ruling coalition stormed the meeting and police detained 49 foreign activists among a number of other people after the gathering was disrupted.
Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim denied the youths acted with government sanction.

Kerry Brogan, Amnesty International's researcher on Indonesia including East Timor, told Reuters by phone from London that she had been told by Australian and East Timorese sources that nine Indonesians were among those Malaysia was deporting.

She said they included Helder da Costa, a lecturer at the University of East Timor currently studying in Adelaide, Australia, Dutch-born human rights activist and lawyer Johannes Princen, and Bambang Surijadi of the unrecognised Indonesia Labour Welfare Union (SBSI).
